title: 2-Year Floating Rate Note auction (second and final reopening of the October new issue) — the congestion rule's second test, in the opposite direction
source: EST: treasury.gov Tentative Schedule of Treasury Auctions PDF (home.treasury.gov/system/files/221/Tentative-Auction-Schedule.pdf), fetched by plain curl 2026-09-09 (HTTP 200, 17,195 bytes) by the treasury-2y-frn-2026-11-24 initial research, text layer decompressed stream-by-stream and re-tokenised into 213 auction records. Row reads `2-Year FRN R / Announcement Thursday, December 17, 2026 / Auction Wednesday, December 23, 2026 / Settlement Monday, December 28, 2026` — the trailing `R` marks it a reopening, and the quarterly cycle (new issue in the last week of Jan/Apr/Jul/Oct, first reopening the following month, second reopening the month after) places it as the SECOND reopening of the 2026-10-28 new issue. Size $28B: the reopening value of sb0590's alternating FRN column, and 20+ consecutive reopenings at $28B since 2024-05-29 (fiscaldata auctions_query, floating_rate:Yes, 154 auctions, HTTP 200, 532,321 bytes, pulled this session). Filed estimate on the two limits this lane records: a tentative schedule is tentative by construction, and this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep — the confirming primary is the 2026-12-17 announcement itself.
notes: DISCOVERED during the treasury-2y-frn-2026-11-24 never-assessed initial research (2026-09-09) and proposed because it is the SECOND discriminating observation for that ledger's headline finding, and it discriminates in the opposite direction from the first. WHY IT EARNS A ROW rather than being left as a downstream footnote: the 11-24 research established, from a join of all 154 FRN auctions against a 4,639-row same-day census of every Treasury auction since 2014, that the FRN's auction closing time is a SAME-DAY CONGESTION rule — four same-day auctions produced `01:00 PM` on 12 of 12 days, three or fewer produced 11:30 AM on 137 of 141 — and not the holiday rule a sibling ledger currently publishes. 2026-11-24 carries FOUR auctions, so the two rules disagree there with congestion predicting 1 p.m. and the holiday reading predicting 11:30. THIS date is the mirror image: the schedule PDF puts THREE auctions on 2026-12-23 (2-Year FRN R, 20-Year BOND R, 17-week bill), so the congestion rule predicts 11:30 AM while the holiday reading predicts 1:00 PM — because 2025-12-23 carried four auctions and did print 1:00 PM. One of the two rules is wrong on 11-24 and the other is wrong on 12-23; together they settle it four weeks apart. SECOND REASON: this is the final reopening of the CUSIP whose two-year coupon spread 2026-10-28 stamps, so it closes out the ~$86B spread-inheritance frame that treasury-2y-frn-2026-10-28 established at 51/51 and 103/103 — that ledger named 11-24 and 12-23 as discovered-and-deliberately-not-filed, and 11-24 has since become a researched event, which makes 12-23 the last unfiled leg rather than one of a pair. INDEX DATE, derivable the same way: the settlement-precedence rule fitted at 152/154 this session gives the Monday 2026-12-21 13-week bill (settles Thursday 2026-12-24) as the index, since 12-24 precedes this FRN's 12-28 settlement — i.e. UNLIKE 2026-11-24, this one's index is set AFTER its own announcement, on the ordinary schedule. DATA TRAP inherited and reproduced: a second reopening files under security_term `1-Year 10-Month`, never `2-Year`, so a `2-Year` filter drops it silently. Proposed as an estimate; `symbols: []` and no house playbook is rates-keyed, so nothing here licenses an entry. Registers nothing of its own — the three forward tests in docs/research/forward-tests/treasury-2y-frn-2026-11-24.md already carry the kill switch this date fires.
